verses.text: Early in the morning Jerub-Baal, that is Gideon, and all his men camped at the spring of Harod. The camp of Midian was north of them in the valley near the hill of Moreh.
The LORD said to Gideon, "You have too many men for me to give Midian into their hands. Israel might boast against me and say, 'We saved ourselves by our own strength.'
So announce to the army, 'Anyone who is afraid and trembling may turn back and leave Mount Gilead.'" So twenty-two thousand men went home, and ten thousand stayed.

But the LORD said to Gideon, "There are still too many men. Take them down to the water, and I will sort them out for you there. If I say, 'This one will go with you,' he will go. But if I say, 'This one will not go with you,' he will not go."
So Gideon took the men down to the water. There the LORD told him, "Separate those who lap the water with their tongues like a dog from those who kneel down to drink."
Three hundred men lapped the water, bringing it to their mouths with their hands. All the rest knelt down to drink.
The LORD said to Gideon, "With the three hundred men who lapped, I will save you and give the Midianites into your hands. Let all the others go home."
So Gideon sent the rest of the Israelites home but kept the three hundred, who took over the food and trumpets of the others. The camp of Midian lay below him in the valley.
That night the LORD said to Gideon, "Get up and go down against the camp, because I have given it into your hands.
If you are afraid to attack, go down to the camp with your servant Purah.
Listen to what they are saying. After that you will feel brave enough to attack the camp." So he and Purah his servant went down to the edge of the camp, where the armed guards were.

The Midianites, the Amalekites and all the other eastern peoples were spread out in the valley, as thick as locusts. Their camels were as many as the grains of sand on the seashore. No one could count them.

Gideon arrived just as a man was telling a friend about his dream. He said, "I had a dream. A round loaf of barley bread came rolling into the Midianite camp. It hit a tent so hard that the tent turned over and fell flat."
His friend answered, "This can only be the sword of Gideon son of Joash, the Israelite. God has given the Midianites and the whole camp into his hands."

When Gideon heard the dream and what it meant, he bowed down and worshipped God. Then he went back to the camp of Israel and called out, "Get up! The LORD has given the Midianite army into your hands!"
He divided the three hundred men into three groups. He gave each man a trumpet and an empty clay jar with a burning torch inside.
He told them, "Watch me and do what I do. When I get to the edge of the camp, do exactly as I do.
When I and all who are with me blow our trumpets, then you also blow your trumpets all around the camp and shout, 'For the LORD and for Gideon!'"

Gideon and the hundred men with him reached the edge of the camp at the beginning of the middle part of the night, just after the guards had been changed. They blew their trumpets and smashed the jars in their hands.
All three groups blew their trumpets and smashed their jars. Holding the torches in their left hands and the trumpets in their right hands, they shouted, "A sword for the LORD and for Gideon!"
Each man stood in his place around the camp. The whole Midianite army ran away, crying out as they fled.

When the three hundred trumpets sounded, the LORD made the men in the camp turn on each other with their swords. The army ran away as far as Beth Shittah toward Zererah, and as far as the border of Abel Meholah near Tabbath.
Israelites from Naphtali, Asher and all Manasseh were called out, and they chased the Midianites.

Gideon sent messengers all through the hill country of Ephraim, saying, "Come down against the Midianites and take control of the waters of the Jordan ahead of them, as far as Beth Barah." So all the men of Ephraim were called out, and they took control of the Jordan as far as Beth Barah.

They also captured two of the Midianite leaders, Oreb and Zeeb. They killed Oreb at the rock of Oreb, and Zeeb at the winepress of Zeeb. They kept chasing the Midianites and brought the heads of Oreb and Zeeb to Gideon, who was by the Jordan.
